content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?NASA Explore The Universe · Join Cosmic Chronicles: Today in Space History · February 24 · Shared with Public groupBack To The Moon After 54 YearsNASA x SpaceXIt’s been 54 years since humans last walked on the Moon during Apollo 17 in 1972. Now, NASA and SpaceX are working together to make it happen again.But here’s the real timeline Artemis IIThis will be the first crewed mission of the Artemis program. Four astronauts will orbit the Moon and return home. No landing yet. This mission must go smoothly. It proves the Space Launch System rocket, the Orion capsule, and all deep space life support systems are ready for longer missions. Starship Human Landing System (HLS)While NASA handles Orion and SLS, SpaceX is building the lunar lander. Starship HLS will not launch directly to the Moon with crew. It will first launch to orbit, refuel in space using tanker Starships, then travel to lunar orbit where astronauts will transfer from Orion into Starship. Starship Version 3 DevelopmentSpaceX is still refining Starship. Version 3 is expected to bring improved engines, heat shield durability, and reliability. Multiple successful orbital flights and refueling demonstrations must happen before NASA puts astronauts on board. In-Space RefuelingThis is one of the biggest technical hurdles. Starship will need multiple tanker launches to fill its tanks in orbit before heading to the Moon. This has never been done at this scale before. Artemis IIIIf Artemis II succeeds and Starship HLS completes all required demonstrations, Artemis III aims to land humans near the lunar south pole. This would mark the first human lunar landing since Apollo.This is not just “we’re going back.”This is building the infrastructure to stay.Apollo proved we could reach the Moon.Artemis is about returning sustainably.And if everything goes according to plan, we’ll witness something historic again.Do you think this timeline holds… or do you expect delays?All reactions:32 sharesLikeCommentShareSee more on FacebookSee more on FacebookEmail or phone numberPasswordLog InForgot password?orCreate new account
